claims.summary: In Korean, it is not necessary to repeat 'I' or 'you' in each sentence when the identity of the participants is already clear. Pronouns of first and second person can be omitted much more easily than in Spanish, especially in conversation and in sequences where the context maintains the same referent.

Korean allows participants to be recovered from context. In '한국어를 공부해요' ('I study Korean'), the speaker can be understood as the subject even if '저는' is not present. Pronouns appear only when they provide contrast, focus, or disambiguation.
The examples provided illustrate how pronouns can be omitted in Korean sentences while maintaining clarity and context, such as '한국어를 공부해요' ('I study Korean') and '어디 가세요?' ('Where are you going?').
